stories.headline: Tamil Nadu Files Review Petition Against Supreme Court Order Allowing Karthigai Lamp Lighting At Thiruparankundram Deepathoon
stories.title: Tamil Nadu Files Review Petition Against Supreme Court Order Allowing Karthigai Lamp Lighting At Thiruparankundram Deepathoon
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Commissioner of Tamil Nadu's Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Department has moved the SupremeCourt seeking a review of the Court's recent order for the lighting of a lamp on the Deepathoon (stone pillar) near a Dargah atop Thiruparankundram hill in Madurai.

It may be recalled that last Friday, the Supreme Court bench comprising Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice Vipul M Pancholi stayed the observations in the Madras High Court judgment permitting the lighting of the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon.
However, as a one-time measure, the Court permitted the lighting of the lamp at the Deepathoon on November 24, the Karthigai Deepam day this year, considering that the proximity of the festival.
The Court clarified that this arrangement should not be construed as a final endorsement of the claimed custom of lighting the lamp at the disputed location.
The bench directed that only authorised representatives of the Devasthanam (temple administration) and government officials would be permitted to access the location for the ritual.
The general public would not be allowed to go to the Deepathoon.
No procession, public congregation, slogan-raising or demonstration shall be allowed during the ceremony.
Further, it directed the authorities to ensure adequate security arrangements and permitted the deployment of the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), if necessary.
It directed the District Collector to file a compliance report within 3 days, and allowed him to approach the Court in case of exigency.

stories.headline: Hemant Soren writes to CJI to urgently appoint Jharkhand HC Chief Justice successor
stories.title: Hemant Soren writes to CJI to urgently appoint Jharkhand HC Chief Justice successor
stories.summary: Jharkhand CM asserted that the High Court of Jharkhand has repeatedly experienced short leadership tenures and interim Acting Chief Justice arrangements at the helm.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'chief justice' in title weight 42
event term: 'chief justice' in summary weight 25.2
article_sentences: Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren has urged Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Supreme Court Collegium to urgently recommend a successor to Jharkhand High Court Chief Justice M.S. Sonak, who is due to retire on November 27.

In a letter to CJI and Judges of the Collegium, Mr. Soren pointed out that frequent transitions accompanied by extended interim arrangements disrupt administrative continuity, affect institutional planning and create uncertainty within the judicial establishment.

“As the Head of the State Government, I am compelled to draw your attention to the fact that an incoming Chief Justice has not been designated nor has any Justice been transferred to the Jharkhand High Court in advance as envisaged under the MoP’ and the Collegium’s statement of February 26, 2026 to assume charge as the Chief Justice on the superannuation of Chief Justice M.S. Sonak on Number 27, 2026,” Mr. Soren wrote in the letter dated November 12, 2026, however shared with media on late night Saturday (November 21, 2026).
Mr. Soren expressed concern that High Court needs stable functioning and regular judicial leadership to maintain public confidence in the administration of justice.

He cited the Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) for appointment of Chief Justices of High Courts which lays down time bound safeguards requiring appointments to be finalised in advance and strictly limiting the tenure of an Acting Chief Justice to ensure that High Courts do not suffer from a leadership vacuum.
He also mentioned that paragraph 3 of the MoP says that initiation of the proposal for the appointment of Chief Justice of a High Court would be by the CJI.
He added that the process of appointment must be initiated well in time to ensure the completion at least one month prior to the date of anticipated vacancy for the Chief Justice of the High Court.

“The CJI would ensure that when a Chief Justice is transferred from one High Court to another simultaneous appointment of his successor in office should be made and ordinarily the arrangement of appointment of an acting Chief justice should not be made for more than one month,” Mr. Soren wrote in the letter.
Jharkhand CM asserted that the High Court of Jharkhand has repeatedly experienced short leadership tenures and interim Acting Chief Justice arrangements at the helm.

“Prior to the appointment of the incumbent Chief Justice, Justice M.S. Sonak on January 9, 2026, the Jharkhand High Court has been adorned by four Chief Justice since the superannuation of Justice Ravi Ranjan on December 19.2022, one of the lordships having a term of a fortnight.
During this period, Acting Chief Justices have been appointed on three occasions for terms ranging from two months to six months,” Mr. Soren said.
He also expressed concern that without the Collegium’s immediate action, the High Court of Jharkhand faces the prospect of yet another interim Acting Chief Justice arrangement.

stories.headline: Supreme Court To Examine Whether Former Mutawalli Can Represent Waqf As Sajjadanashin After Tenure Ends
stories.title: Supreme Court To Examine Whether Former Mutawalli Can Represent Waqf As Sajjadanashin After Tenure Ends
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has agreed to examine the question of whether a former Mutawalli (caretaker of waqf) can continue representing a Waqf in legal proceedings after the expiry of his tenure by claiming that he is also a Sajjadanashin (spiritual head of a shrine).

A Bench of Justice Manoj Misra and Justice Vijay Bishnoi was hearing a plea challenging the Karnataka High Court's Kalaburagi Bench judgment, which allowed a suit filed by the Dargah to continue through a Waqf Officer after the petitioner's tenure as Mutawalli expired.

The dispute arose after the Waqf Tribunal dismissed the Dargah's suit seeking a declaration that certain properties were Waqf properties, on the ground that the person representing it no longer held the position of Mutawalli.
The High Court set aside the dismissal, holding that the suit had been instituted in the name of the Waqf institution and should not fail merely because its Mutawalli's tenure had ended.
It directed that the proceedings continue through the Waqf Officer.

Before the Supreme Court, the petitioner challenging the High Court's judgment argued that he could continue representing the Dargah because he was also a Sajjadanashin, an office which does not carry a fixed tenure.

The Court observed that the issue was whether, in the absence of a Waqfnama or any custom pleaded in the original proceedings establishing the petitioner's position as Sajjadanashin, he could continue representing the Dargah after his appointment as Mutawalli had expired.

“What is relevant to be considered is whether in absence of any Waqfnama or a Waqf deed, and in absence of any custom pleaded in the plaint/application preferred before the Tribunal by the petitioner of him being the Sajjadanashin of the Dargah concerned, having accepted his appointment as a Mutawalli, could he continue to represent the Waqf/Dargah on expiry of his term as the Mutawalli.”, the Court noted.
For deciding the issue, the bench has listed the matter for further hearing on November 25, seeking assistance from the petitioner's counsel.
